content: We follow recent work on constructing challenge datasets for probing neural models, which has primarily focused on the task of natural language inference (NLI) BIBREF14, BIBREF15, BIBREF16, BIBREF17, BIBREF18. Most of this work looks at constructing data through adversarial generation methods, which have also been found useful for creating stronger models BIBREF19. There has also been work on using synthetic data of the type we consider in this paper BIBREF20, BIBREF21, BIBREF22. We closely follow the methodology of BIBREF22, who use hand-constructed linguistic fragments to probe NLI models and study model re-training using a variant of the inoculation by fine-tuning strategy of BIBREF23. In contrast, we focus on probing open-domain MCQA models (see BIBREF24 for a related study in the reading comprehension setting) as well as constructing data from much larger sources of structured knowledge.
